panels.description:
The **input**: a flat call table, one row per caller/callee pair with a count. This is the shape Prometheus, Loki and SQL actually return — the rows already describe edges, but the column names do not match the node-graph convention and there is no `id` column.

Note `api -> db` and `db -> api` form a cycle, on purpose: the reshaped output is therefore also a sankey adversarial fixture.

gateway,api,1200

api,db,900
auth,db,300
db,api,120

panels.title: Input — flat call table

panels.description:
The **edges frame**, produced by a SQL Expression over query A. Renames `caller`/`callee` to `source`/`target`, synthesises the required `id`, and casts the count to a number for `mainstat`.

The `CAST` matters: SQL Expressions run **server-side, before** frontend transformations, so a `convertFieldType` transformation cannot be used to prepare data for them. `csv_content` delivers untyped columns, and MySQL `CAST` is a no-op on a value that is already numeric — so casting is safe regardless of source.

targets.csvContent:
caller,callee,calls
gateway,api,1200
gateway,web,800
api,auth,650
api,db,900
auth,db,300
db,api,120
web,api,450

targets.expression:
SELECT CONCAT(caller, '->', callee) AS id,
       caller AS source,
       callee AS target,
       CAST(calls AS DECIMAL(20, 4)) AS mainstat
FROM A

panels.title: Reshaped — edges frame

panels.description:
The **nodes frame**, produced by a second SQL Expression over the same query A. Both endpoint columns are `UNION`ed and de-duplicated so a service appearing as both caller and callee yields one node.

This frame is **optional** — Grafana derives the node set from `source`/`target` when no nodes frame is present. Add it when nodes need titles, subtitles or their own stats.

targets.csvContent:
caller,callee,calls
gateway,api,1200
gateway,web,800
api,auth,650
api,db,900
auth,db,300
db,api,120
web,api,450

targets.expression:
SELECT DISTINCT n.id AS id, n.id AS title
FROM (SELECT caller AS id FROM A
      UNION
      SELECT callee AS id FROM A) AS n

panels.title: Reshaped — nodes frame

panels.description:
Both reshaped frames feeding a node graph. Query A is hidden — it still executes because the expressions reference it, but it is not displayed.

**This is the case that forces field-shape detection.** The two frames reaching the panel are named `B` and `C` by refId; they are not called `nodes`/`edges`, and a SQL Expression cannot set `meta.preferredVisualisationType`. Of Grafana's three node-graph detection signals, only field shape survives — `B` is the edges frame because it carries `source`, `C` is nodes because it does not.

Rendered with the core Node graph panel; the ECharts relations panel beside it reads the identical frames.

Requires the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle (GA, on by default). Not available on 32-bit ARM hosts; arm64 including Apple Silicon is fine.

panels.description:
The same two SQL Expression frames, rendered by the **ECharts relations panel**. Nothing about the queries changes — this panel runs the same field-shape detection (`isEdgesFrame` / `isNodesFrame` in `converters/nodeGraph.ts`), so `B` is read as edges and `C` as nodes purely from their columns.

Switch **Chart type** to `sankey` or `chord` to see the other variants over the identical frames. Note the input contains a cycle (`api -> db`, `db -> api`), so the sankey variant will report a dropped link.
